name: Mumbai

character.name: Kaju the crow

intro.text: Arre, new face at my tapri? Everybody here, I know. Let's see if you're from here.

outro.text: Achha, achha. Let's see where you stand, boss.

character.voice: ElevenLabs Voice Design: quick, sharp, cheeky young Mumbai man, Indian English with easy Hinglish, warm and fast

test.tip: Two short beats, both even: "HAAN, CHA-lo". Let the "aa" in haan go through your nose a little.

ok.text: Thoda shy, yaar. Say it like you mean it.

bad.text: Arre, are you asking me or telling me?

test.tip: Give every syllable the same weight: "ek CUT-ting CHAI, BHAI-ya". Tap the T in cutting with your tongue curled back a bit.

good.text: One cutting, coming! You've done this before, na?

ok.text: Close, boss. Little faster, like you've got a train to catch.

bad.text: One what? Speak up, yaar, the kettle is louder than you!

test.line: Arre yaar, traffic mein phas gaya tha.
test.meaning: Oh man, I got stuck in traffic.
accepted: arre yaar traffic mein phas gaya tha
are yaar traffic mein phas gaya tha
arre yar traffic mein phas gaya tha
are yar traffic main phas gaya tha
arre yaar traffic me phas gaya tha
arey yaar traffic mein fas gaya tha
are yaar traffic mein fus gaya tha
arre yaar traffic mein phans gaya tha
are you traffic mein phas gaya tha
test.tip: Keep an even rhythm, one beat per syllable, and let "arre yaar" sound a bit fed up: "ar-RE YAAR".

good.text: Hahaha, every Mumbaikar's excuse! Full marks.

ok.text: Achha, I believe the traffic. Not fully the accent.

bad.text: Stuck where? You sound like you came straight from the airport!

celebration.text: Arre, total tourist! No tension, we'll make you a Mumbaikar.
Not bad, yaar! You're a proper visitor now.
Wah! You could live in my building, boss!
Ekdum first class! Full Mumbaikar, no doubt!

setting: Low-poly Mumbai street on a warm evening: old buildings with balconies and shutters, a chai tapri by the station, an auto-rickshaw, string lights and plants, no rain.
